{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the belly line of the fish, the whole lower outline from the nose to the tail end, in several short runs of 5 to 7 dominoes each. It carried the fall from the start all the way to the tail join, so the lower half of the fish stands in the picture. The final table has about 109 of 110 dominoes connected to the start by eye, and the fish reads as a fish.

Execution: I traced stroke 2 from the pad as sketched, so it branched off the line near the nose and stayed gentle and connected. I inspected the belly area twice to check for breaks. I cleared the few stray dominoes under the top line by the dip, since they would never fall, and left the line itself untouched. After that I kept my hands off the table so nobody bumped it before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed with short updates on the belly status, the strays I cleared, and when I was hands off. I left the tail join to Sofia and Jack so we did not double up on the same stretch. I backed the agreement to stop adding anything and protect the finished line.

Leadership: I kept the mood light and steady in the last minutes. I called the hands-off point early and followed it myself, which helped the table stay calm and avoid last-minute bumps. I took clear ownership of the belly and reported when it was finished so others could plan around it.

I believe my share of the table's result was about 30 percent. The belly was a large, necessary part of the outline, and I built it reliably, though the table's result came from all four of us.", "my_share_percent": 30}
